C7A3876321FE45A899DF3F08528C614D.description: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

C29B136A812D445A9D82AC4FAB850E30.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

2D3BEF85D8694FDF97CD1CDAF2EBC639.description: Construct inscribed and circumscribed circles for polygons and tangent lines from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

1776B05AFCF84DB1BD3CE0D97C45EB9B.description: Construct inscribed and circumscribed circles for triangles.

FF3669F7044246FFBE7F067F3DC21271.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

0BAC7C6D276A43AE87CE47B0E679F25E.description: Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g. surveying problems, resultant forces).

315B6FF7D22C402F84AF1338FD75DC0C.description: Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

45CEF2F0CDBF4DC0852469E0146715FB.description: Derive the formula A = ½ ab sin C for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

63D1089125FB4EE49F1C4C12563E32FE.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

7C30C4AAC9764E55BD8B3C20E7C6CDC8.description: Construct arguments about triangles using theorems. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity, and AA.

5C802E3F2A6A4CF9BB47B85026077C75.description: Construct arguments about theorems involving similarity.

C187D69080BD41E28FC4C42C86F67D9B.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

B90CB4EB4479476BA585FE3489A000E6.description: Demonstrate triangle congruence using rigid motion (ASA, SAS, and SSS).

3A34A760059A436090FBB1401F3F03B6.description: Given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

E25BCDBAF6D641F4941BBEF6A6D71832.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

647C9E100BB34F28A26F99CA1046F139.description: Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them to solve problems.

0D6EE7D867B44DDDBCB35376DAB9E2F0.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin (θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant.

7856E723A71D4B249499576EE8996709.description: Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.

5FC68CC3729846DABDC497F4826E5DBE.description: Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.

907C32D1D0504504B7EA53391E4CF481.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

85E8D1FFC0034DCE9BCCCDF176B0E1F3.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

B612B4B1644D42D285139F033F6B7A36.description: Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

43E5EF217B0E481797528D99DAB5EF1A.description: Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4, and π/6, use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π - x, π + x, and 2π - x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

4CF21F515986478C91261986CCEB4EFC.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

99C1191E9208423D82B305820D869340.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

D5D71918FE614A77AFC46F12E4519ECA.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

F294B5AF295D4FA6B07BB291A978E578.description: Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the domain.

3BB2C227CC89443BA6E67DED7774F9D2.description: Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

BC4E089CD6EE456D9606BAF1365CC751.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

0AF54DCC9E8C44B1997463C65F8E7725.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences and series both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

4F7D0C31FBB9410595A3CAB7F8CAE258.description: Use functions to model real-world relationships.

92FA4FE1141D4C98BCDD17C13A27B036.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

1E64B52DB876493B9D394791C81030BF.description: Compare properties of two functions using a variety of representations (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

3BE5467684D7468AB09881CB650869B3.description: Write a function in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

EA7A27C1783D4BF48851A5929E828018.description: Graph trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

15AB4BD464F24902958B1F7D4B92EF22.description: Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

AD50A63972EA489C809C2FA9313633D8.description: Graph piecewise-defined functions, including step functions.

727B006E61C94F92B2BA5BE2C2BF52F2.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

ED954EAF344A4D1DA5A43B8034376AD4.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

D02E856D6F784460A6445A8DA66C113C.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of expressions, graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

5D82F3D353704843BC3E3725C8F09FAE.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

7F7321AC07204ADEB738B89CF48F2522.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

EBA47B2192B04227A7D5B9828D2ADD4B.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

097EF22AE9124904A5E84A7FB6809F3F.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

FDBA6CD1B09A47A38081EAACF2ED2D87.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

4E6E043F031B4953B09703C020D4ABAA.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

1B2BADA011F24418B071FE5C42676247.description: Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation and solve (incorporating technology) for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater.

58A69743579049668C30551931633A75.description: Apply and extend previous understanding to solve equations, inequalities, and compound inequalities in one variable, including literal equations and inequalities. (A.REI.3)

7F48CE9C700145AFB20CDEAAF18BA859.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

9071B81AA18F439C9F0CB2316DDC4194.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

B38CA1E6660B4981B1E592FA101CFED6.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

FB44433F8EEB4CBD98B688DD61B6AC81.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

9656B4911EFA42AFAD1313C17BAA8055.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

0ADF918EC209439A8D5331EC856DA1C5.description: Apply and extend previous understanding to create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

AC1319CFCC784C539EEBB2AF73BB3827.description: Apply and extend previous understanding to create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems.

C406B0A00313496B8EDEC1A1273AF305.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

EB209C7CA4B24457AD5E69B36A94C974.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

98ADA0D66C9A491BAFD5EF5854089E36.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

A33EF7250F464D76B02087AF93605A65.description: Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)² in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle. The Binomial Theorem can be proven by mathematical induction or by a combinatorial argument.

4FBB6177803043E5B41970AC4716C732.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

DB9B99738BBE49449C49D4DE68FBC290.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

DA21B921EDA2494EBB53E7A41EF161E8.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

1E7BC43DA67C437986EA322DCE9BB727.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

E471214769354DD78918B2AB9077DDF3.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

86107B3C7EA54160B2755D97CA0F4633.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

F4AB47C3DBCF4CABB2C4C02C28399DB7.description: Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

B4D95C023FB0422CAA5E2CE55DDFCCCB.description: Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

44B8CEA303FF426F853021F84D78C605.description: Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

4CB66F8C8DB0450696E48A38C175BAE7.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

9EA48F3A8B874F22921DEEE2897C6EFA.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

407DDA87E02348FAA1DD35E3D0CD97C2.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, (e.g. as c(v<sub>x</sub>, v<sub>y</sub>) = (cv<sub>x</sub>, cv<sub>y</sub>).)

63FBDC751D734B679A1FA19E333A269E.description: Multiply a vector by a scalar.

E2EE04C3B60A4AB988E383BD1911EAD0.description: Understand vector subtraction v - w as v + (-w), where –w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

1DA4B5AB1F58408F9CD254B9EE082AAC.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

CBEE416336BE41DCB455ED8CFE8B39C7.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule . Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

994F8A8311344EF9B852F81941C98241.description: Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

5E3903A69445434CB0D0682E9AE3872C.description: Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

B8A40DBD6D384A10893DF7F95DCC6C11.description: Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

8C90434F34994382A4232C0D52B020DF.description: Represent and model with vector quantities.

94DCD85BE6E24A3EAB668D9520C7BD02.description: Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

26C80C71D8254AEA8E71F633E5FBA985.description: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.

2206E40875DA4E65B6F43133D216ED68.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

7F3D5A9A6E9D482FB4F03C1D06A90126.description: Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

F798C2D4A5D14BD494DE4D35318D9C5A.description: Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.

3C06B56767484D94990FC8767FC0DBB4.description: Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.

FF50873A82C3431BBF73E1AD9CB8C1BA.description: Represent complex numbers and their operations on the complex plane.

E5DC0E22EC024FE49E89035001292E12.description: Use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.

E61C65DC3FAE4F6AA48F6A618E1BE3C5.description: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers.

C189EC4B858947ECBD4930FFD9C07749.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

5E6029B4749F4A6DB3FBBDB8EB8B538A.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

004D04AC9DE44BEC8B59C99D8960D002.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

2A3E2D45ACC64041BDFF717D23EDDC3B.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

7A680EEE67C246889604EE77992F6295.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

CE81A67B72A34B188D1796EDC30B6726.description: Look for and make use of structure.

CA586E85B388457B9BFFA115A2A381D1.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

B5A4806391704AB69531B25F7CCE4485.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Kansas Mathematics Standards

9E7AE726578C4C40AFE52C25A74E73D6.description: Relating the choice of measures of center and variability to the distribution of the data.

2EB16ECB9E07428294BC16C92351A671.description: Giving quantitative measures of center (mean, median and/or mode) and variability (range and/or interquartile range), as well as describing any overall pattern and any striking deviations from the overall pattern with reference to the context in which the data were gathered.

B14432C344644C98817EAC07EA38AFE4.description: Describing the nature of the attribute under investigation, including how it was measured and its units of measurement.

198AE9715D4B4F74B607AF67A1516857.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, such as by:

9F713E2404644618ACF0ECE11732E59A.description: Display numerical data on dot plots, histograms, stem-and-leaf plots, and box plots. (6.SP.4)

33E56D78109D4A6C82031A57E0334EAF.description: Recognize that a measure of center (mean, median and/or mode) for a numerical data set summarizes all of its values with a single number, while a measure of variation (range and/or interquartile range) describes how its values vary with a single number.

C31B021A94A040199A8C0E52A38FF2B6.description: Analyze a set of data collected to answer a statistical question with a distribution which can be described by its center (mean, median and/or mode), spread (range and/or interquartile range), and overall shape (cluster, peak, gap, symmetry, skew (data) and/or outlier).

CFFC55E390E746D0B17D1F16BC3AAE50.description: Recognize and generate a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data related to the question and accounts for it in the answers.

5590FC5BA9644BFEA3BF9FDD39994582.description: Develop concepts of statistical measures of center and variability and an informal understanding of outlier.

885C9E5BD20446DF835DCC2666AA6F79.description: Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation.

6B7A6828A1104E72BB1D8E6D24098959.description: Write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable.

ADC563E6C1014385B3BFB5D83DC6669D.description: Identify the independent and dependent variable.

E5616B5A307240F4B454907F55D25C56.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another.

726CCA6778FD4CDDA08B04F36202C697.description: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables.

DFC5953E9158459C90806DE23B04C556.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint or condition in a real-world or mathematical problem. Recognize that inequalities of the form x > c or x < c have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions of such inequalities on number line diagrams.

69569C1FA02D466887EC861CD62C614C.description: Solve one-step equations involving non-negative rational numbers using addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

265EDA10B20B4740AEF91ACF812851B8.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving a real-world or mathematical problem; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number, or, depending on the purpose at hand, any number in a specified set.

96B84E86D68A4C94848A522EFA5C2739.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering a question: which values from a specified set, if any, make the equation or inequality true? Use substitution to determine whether a given number in a specified set makes an equation or inequality true.

939477D90E3842009DA1F2777CB5563D.description: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities.

EC74AE65DF384F8EAF2C0183031D251D.description: Apply the properties of operations and combine like terms, with the conventions of algebraic notation, to identify and generate equivalent expressions.

5DAD891F00164E1FBA1E348D9426DD2B.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of their variables. Include expressions that arise from formulas used in real-world problems. Perform arithmetic operations, including those involving whole-number exponents, in the conventional order when there are no parentheses to specify a particular order (Order of Operations).

18926F4D5971465FA7C446719F504ABB.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient); view one or more parts of an expression as a single entity.

469976265B6D407F9B86CD64488D2D47.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

212CD7CD0C07472FA2DA9DAA072EE108.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

8F2E9FF7366D418B853B2EDEA88F2E09.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

82FED8CCB34A4F32B5C74C4333F908E1.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions.

CA25DDC132534684AE34EC357E1F3470.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane. Include use of coordinates and absolute value to find distances between points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate.

7124060D6E804602AD55B2B95B62248A.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

BA0A387B11694207B16CFF2CE6194F33.description: Explain the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from 0 on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude for a positive or negative quantity in a real-world situation.

2E1EFF7548224EB9BCAFD3C21318AC0C.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

76F0CD702F5A48EFAAD9FA2776E9A2E1.description: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.

0980ED567C38428295665E7A8F06C773.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

58E870E77D0F42AFB8CE101868A4D88A.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram; find and position pairs of integers and other rational numbers on a coordinate plane.

FB6F75C83FDB44A6BA11B846E949CBCC.description: Recognize signs of numbers in ordered pairs indicate locations in quadrants of the coordinate plane; recognize that when two ordered pairs differ only by signs, the locations of the points are related by reflections across one or both axes.

07A9B9026B3142E6854438D38D37C641.description: Recognize opposite signs of numbers as indicating locations on opposite sides of 0 on the number line; recognize that the opposite of the opposite of a number is the number itself, (e.g. -(-3)=3) and that 0 is its own opposite.

5645A7B83EEB42F6A43E28257B0E1200.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line and a coordinate pair as a location on a coordinate plane.

49932735588C4846A6071BFD75E83071.description: Explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.

A9199D2661DC404F86D5900D53B006B9.description: Use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts,

CB281198EEF64C93809F90197FC5AD29.description: Understand positive and negative numbers to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g. temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge);

EE75F4919AA14343A6BBD7774CB893DA.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers.

6E5BEBC8EC7B4EC08083BA87E29001F1.description: Find the greatest common factor of two whole numbers less than or equal to 100 and the least common multiple of two whole numbers less than or equal to 12. Use the distributive property to express a sum of two whole numbers 1–100 with a common factor as a multiple of a sum of two whole numbers with no common factor.

3F9ACA7BD3794A799C8151E1909A60E0.description: Fluently (efficiently, accurately, and flexibly) add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using an efficient algorithm for each operation.

D2F7822DBC3B477DB930FF929D1C032A.description: Fluently (efficiently, accurately, and flexibly) divide multi-digit numbers using an efficient algorithm.

A930398C89774885B23671C9A804BEAE.description: Compute fluently (efficiently, accurately, and flexibly) with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples.

190574FDC44744AB83773B145E289B6D.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, requiring multiple exposures connecting various concrete and abstract models.

9E798EEAB33E4F0C8E35F9864B6965DE.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions.

AE9778D526D04AB196D9E32B81739790.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units; manipulate and transform units appropriately when multiplying or dividing quantities.

1B8E5B9ADBF9455CA31659F73426F2A4.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g. 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

BFD622E12AFD4A4B8075AF3C8F02A5DA.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find the missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios. Solve unit rate problems including those involving unit pricing and constant speed.

48340619CC4E497EA9EF73C301D15D76.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, (e.g. by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagram, or using calculations.)

F729014896B04849971858A582BF27AF.description: Use unit rate language ("for each one", "for every one" and "per") and unit rate notation to demonstrate understanding the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b≠0,

81D5802D017E4641BAC65D6B5D150FEF.description: Use ratio language to describe a relationship between two quantities. Distinguish between part-to-part and part-to-whole relationships.

F57DF5D3A9F04301AE8FF24189E83049.description: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems.

1B7ABCE0720B47ACB74D9EAABD71A741.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles, and use the nets to find the surface area of these figures. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

321E9B34F51F4E4EA6DFF3509A32F782.description: Draw polygons whose edges meet at right angles (rectilinear figure polygons) in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find the length of a side joining points with the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate. Apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

35EF112EF66249D3AFF4F4459C710C51.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by applying the formulas V=lwh and V=Bh (B is the area of the base and h is the height) to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with fractional edge lengths in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

84414BEBAB29400E997C86C7B88633E1.description: Find the area of all triangles, special quadrilaterals (including parallelograms, kites and trapezoids), and polygons whose edges meet at right angles (rectilinear figure polygons) by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

761AFDCF0EB241B295F9BE65895FBCD8.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

63E44C8D49154513957DF42953E895FC.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

3ED851B27199414D976C16791805F697.description: Look for and make use of structure.

0BFED80E77B64A049E620D5B76BD015D.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

E7A0F1BBAE584D34ABB16724BFD02F35.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Kansas Mathematics Standards

E4DA6988C0B144D585AA93BDB7655133.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

AE5B225F0A184DD789354B84B640C578.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g. "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

A32EC56059FA4191A4DBC9E10644DDED.description: Know that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

FC09B641645F43FAA3837C98FA40709A.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

3187563B61504DC5AEA4EC69886BDCD3.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.

BBBAE72C134E42EBBEEBCF318CB651D8.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

9AB2F37D110C4C48A80941AA4B5E3005.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

C4D3780C08434E3883E83BA4A8315D33.description: Collect data from a chance process (probability experiment). Approximate the probability by observing its long-run relative frequency. Recognize that as the number of trials increase, the experimental probability approaches the theoretical probability. Conversely, predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.

3A88AE5FBCF94F708C838FCA8A8448D9.description: Express the probability of a chance event as a number between 0 and 1 that represents the likelihood of the event occurring. (Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around ½ indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.)

5780B113737F4286A72B279A5069A053.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

CC7D4CE3983846E9AC8D4E80878D141D.description: Use measures of center (mean, median and/or mode) and measures of variability (range, interquartile range and/or mean absolute deviation) for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

31D04D7C796E40808DE0826960B2568C.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability (requires introduction of mean absolute deviation).

F6E585F19AD64F189B9017BC12C72302.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

14EEB2A359F5470087231023017DC4FE.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to informally gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.

E677EE9516B04722AAD1BA3D28EB5768.description: Identify if a particular random sample would be representative of a population and justify your reasoning.

2D047BACA1D34F0CA069F2BAE1018387.description: Know that generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population and generate a valid representative sample of a population.

277A1876AC6D466A867906CCF035220E.description: Use statistics to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population;

31A17D6344964C4DB9FF6434E4C86B34.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

0FA7D89AEC6445CFA65998EB10AEBCEE.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px+q > r or px+q < r where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers and p > 0. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.

83F27AB588644DABA359854B350F66E8.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px+q=r, and p(x+q)=r where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently (efficiently, accurately, and flexibly). Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.

13BC2826B3964C5E808B6650B35CA86A.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct two-step equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

AB58BF6E5A53416296140FF24A8D243C.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems with rational numbers. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

EFF9A58B2AEB48C7B4111E86C8F9587E.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

B9AE733317BF423691B5945738E8F403.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.

CE7E027841774FCEA8F2D4F60280C29F.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with integer coefficients.

484A40204072435ABE0FFDF98F643222.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

0D37CAE901E14180B526EEBB4775D8BB.description: Solve and interpret real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.

29DEA105CCAD4751A8FB9856180A0A80.description: Convert a rational number in the form of a fraction to its decimal equivalent using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

668C2F9B4A814EEF95D476EE69A65A62.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

FA4E2787753A492E8FC2610E3C24C080.description: Explain that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. Leading to situations such that if p and q are integers, then -(p/q)=(-p)/q=p/(-q).

9595F63E5B3A43188BD198561302F844.description: Describe how multiplication is extended from positive rational numbers to all rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (-1)(-1)=1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers.

60768BBBC62E4BDBB909EFD06A2A7621.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division of positive rational numbers to multiply and divide all rational numbers.

7B6A4AAFF5334AAAAE545284CE8FFB0A.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

81B07394324B473B8B008628FA77A24E.description: Model subtraction as the distance between two rational numbers on the number line where the distance is the absolute value of their difference.

1B6A93570A6A4E35AECB69C51AB55383.description: Model subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p-q=p+(-q).

F411C3A5E66F49268C4EED145A551617.description: Show p+q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative.

2801F8EEF32F4E3C9843C6DC2A03B1DF.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses).

CCDE74E440194E6682EEC5D8D2CB02E4.description: Represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

572851ACFA6840528635A03D54670317.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with positive rational numbers to add, subtract, multiply, and divide all rational numbers.

FECC9B6D9CE144E2AA07B11791B2EE0B.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems. Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.

C3DC8C3C673B45B3AD218980F1DFA51E.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

D213FE3551BB4DF591033592D81CA149.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations. For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t=pn.

30AEF46DE5A14966B18A7F7B1301010E.description: Analyze a table or graph and recognize that, in a proportional relationship, every pair of numbers has the same unit rate (referred to as the "m").

84084B639B9A4B48ABD6578775ACF31B.description: Determine whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g. by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

D946DD4E1B6C4300B79931459F723FE3.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities:

1206A27632C74460801D0F6CFE796C29.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units.

00359EBBAAB24FCD9F2127092F0F2876.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

D0981AF52FBF4A8193F61358707AF4AA.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right cylinder.

907FA9E639CD48EABFDCCA95473AC80C.description: Identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotating a two-dimensional (rectangular or triangular) object around one edge.

BEC978CCCD3C4B3886B8ED99C8331DC5.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, such as computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

D946F1244B77438CADAB67E3664E496C.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

F09B1AFBDC334FB0829D888AFBBF5B15.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area of two-dimensional objects and volume and surface area of three-dimensional objects including cylinders and right prisms. (Solutions should not require students to take square roots or cube roots.

60573F4D8CB94A948B82AC879DC2A7A4.description: Generalize the surface area formula for prisms and cylinders (SA = 2B + Ph where B is the area of the base, P is the perimeter of the base, and h is the height (in the case of a cylinder, perimeter is replaced by circumference)).

6297A0198563428F9D15CF498A4A1A42.description: Generalize the volume formula for prisms and cylinders (V = Bh where B is the base and h is the height).

0D665E75B64E4A92AABCBECE47629AA8.description: Investigate the relationship between three-dimensional geometric shapes;

0AB6AD7A2EBD400AA5223E039747481A.description: .Use the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

A5AE94DDF5E841EF8474DED01A4584B7.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

AEB1C189C13A4A1D92D5C8833930723B.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

AA14AC2A17374F59BDF118DD91ADA2D9.description: Look for and make use of structure.

C9123035C6704561923E0BCF06FD78A5.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

AFA2A4FE85B349D99454660B35C8C6B7.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Kansas Mathematics Standards

DCED4B925BA449058ECB7733AF26F37C.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g. product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

E9CCE712015549749D98719D8DD075D3.description: Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g. drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

B70B63578E9847A4A39ADD30FA7A5E27.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.

E674DB963F4F460694AEAF48673A16F9.description: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance.

5749D90C04954CB68CA1D9C177F5F3EE.description: Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.

042B23B4B94E412B8E9A354F373FA091.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.

369AC8151C2A4A47AC07CCD9939D41B4.description: Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value.

2CF70B1B4889436BBB4B1513BC7270CE.description: Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value.

249AA402301C42D2916E42D70513FAFE.description: Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.

341DF0B330124CF889927DAF16FC28DE.description: Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

A2E131A7DDA746F5862472849060C872.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.

F1393AD62BE5429F92A69ABB0D83B19C.description: Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

16F3C7B0B19942D2AEF7A291A0EFF373.description: Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B│A) = P(B)P(A│B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

C8D4C88CE0D54BF1B668DC1B08793022.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

D68C5AC6E244430C9FEF011F3CE72243.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

E2C537C3A3294DB18F9779C0C7F56176.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

B982BF76263343008B416216372EAB13.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.

A7EC1867884B46A5BB5796D478D8C4EB.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

428041877A2742C7B3C5AE96DCA37E54.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B) , and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

D8AA949C4C9D41819145D90B53927CF0.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

38A4EDBA89DE404A94CE3B6FE474FFFB.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

BEB9344FA51346CEADE5037643590972.description: Understand independent and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

5BD62893382F422EB50B48A743627C45.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

82C4455FBB2F4701BBE527331957ABCC.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

3777F428427B42E3AC49DE3EF5A2EE1A.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error, (e.g. through the use of simulation models for random sampling.)

CCDD2F99EE5C4F86A19EABAB9D2E2910.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

B5CAD0F2E77F4D5197CEF4249FCE36C7.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.

791D95233C7A4F3EB01070FBFFD26154.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g. using simulation.

DB022DDE38A24B2D8471228D739DFBD5.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences to be made about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

025829FB893241ECAEA06FA68EF50D40.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

26D7018F47094FE88BEA379952D3F5BD.description: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.

3051C7BC291045B08EB26BEB90D4E1A6.description: Fit quadratic and exponential functions to the data. Use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data.

91BEE253193E4EDC98DE31E8B031E9C1.description: Assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

6FE6DE4863384794BDD89856AA1EBFCF.description: Fit a linear function to data and use it to solve problems in the context of the data.

7A161B506F584FCE85FACBABF0FC389E.description: Use a given linear function to solve problems in the context of data.

6C40361549F142FFADF0144892016081.description: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.

CF15612A5847438DB760AB1435A7422E.description: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.

3BD3EA9AA56E44148876A559D0F3AEC3.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

A74FC71247CA48DF9E862D43D55320D1.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.
