48DDD667BC96408F9092F87076B8AA59.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

73406BB1D522492993530AABB2B3CD3D.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

DA9B9E2F8E024EF8BF7C13F16A5F161A.description: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.

C63B8EA1328244BF9C39999C29DE4ABC.description: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems.

953A0CE8086741559C6A6BF4E14CAD89.description: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical and algebraic expressions.

A003F7000A4A458F8C3364D45050D095.description: Use properties of rational numbers and irrational numbers.

10EF9629DF234E47BEA28B6A7DCCB299.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

A0720231ECE74F5B865284ED0D7C15F2.description: Look for and make use of structure.

2F184B3A0575478998426B8105B0C385.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

49DABAC6D8B14EB986129B9A7BEF5263.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Kansas Mathematics Standards

C046FD8D492A46D8BF7ADA1968877A5A.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two decimals refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the relational symbols >, < =, or ≠, and justify the conclusions, (e.g. by using a visual model.).

76627041C15C4BD9B506EA5443A00D2C.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

312D8317820D477CB17AF7FE8B773593.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.

48673278FE3E4FDCA1C893B9ADAF99B0.description: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions.

640D49F9FDD74E64937CC35076DDC6D5.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number.

B03C6D2DAD314B0699CA250D68FF59E1.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

DDF65C3539FE4C46BF03B4E4CE0C1ED1.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.

939378FDF6184215B6099E6C47354C93.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

9D0D8C1E77FF49719F5EA3466DAE67DF.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g. by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

B1F7BD3285BE4993B8D0EE0C6D9E6293.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g. by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction (simplest form is not an expectation), and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

2811EFD31E5E47D18071426E60023909.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g. by using a visual fraction model.

2741396C20F24BCCB451DDFF07FE7567.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

4482B5AFA1FA4FAD81129CAB88CCD6F3.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

F31E9EE7A5BC4E83AAAB7DF98D94E257.description: Build fractions from unit fractions by applying and extending previous understandings of operations on whole numbers.

DBC1AEAB34844B54BB1DB6059D003C59.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators, (e.g. by creating common numerators or denominators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as ½.) Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with relational symbols >, <, =, or ≠, and justify the conclusions, (e.g. by using visual fraction models.).

87A8E05701A94DA3AD6632E265E7D590.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction ((n·a))/((n·b) ) by using visual fraction models, with attention to how the number and size of the parts differ even though the two fractions themselves are the same size. Use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.

F904D7A5DE304EA5AF16D8D887BFCBAA.description: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering.

7521AB70035245ACA0DB189EAD18247A.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

613ADAA0A63A49D4990544FE5ABF042B.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles (right, acute, obtuse, straight, reflex). Recognize and categorize triangles based on angles (acute, obtuse, equiangular, and right) and/or sides (scalene, isosceles, and equilateral).

65E9C55A738349FDBEE3A7204F5F2195.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse, straight, reflex), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.

D60EB2F9F69545F8AF27A92A4F2BD842.description: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.

2E1F401DD79D4C6F8DAE8F91B7906AE6.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems explaining and justifying the appropriate unit of measure.

BB83061F0D0649B7995C451EF8B5E7C2.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals, and problems that require expressing measurements given in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams that feature a measurement scale.

D5685B02AE584C69B4AC9C00E0BBA342.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units including km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz; l, ml; hr, min, sec. Within a single system of measurement, express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit. Record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.

B82ADF73F72041F1BFD69968CF71076D.description: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements from a larger unit to a smaller unit.

6DBFE4C0647949F8BB10D46D9180EE01.description: Make a data display (line plot, bar graph, pictograph) to show a set of measurements in fractions of a unit (½, ¼, 1/8, 1/16). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in the data display.

023E7687557349F28C06ADB0329444DC.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

2AE0518D24734DD0A259581A1DF61DBC.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.

BB501AFD75C74ED899DB92B6BFA0C832.description: Fluently (efficiently, accurately, and flexibly) add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using an efficient algorithm (including, but not limited to: traditional, partial-sums, etc.), based on place value understanding and the properties of operations.

9EA5E5B0FE354D7394EC28622019FAAE.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

29F8EFA4393445D7A68DD6F9DC7B9702.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

F892CC68BCBF43F4B0B66E98EA75D23B.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, expanded form, and unit form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place, using >, <, =, and ≠ symbols to record the results of comparisons.

F9E35C87811A46B3A7BBD0E500411E3A.description: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

8D6CAE3CC59940D2B5CB8997010F98AC.description: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers.

8CBCC5B251CE4AE99404A66427A5B850.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

C0FAB6F7001F43A2A36A6AC7AAFB2DD2.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself. For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 1, generate terms in the resulting sequence and observe that the terms appear to alternate between odd and even numbers. Explain informally why the numbers will continue to alternate in this way.

C68F23C9C1C746F8BC2060C9CE6F82F9.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1 to 100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1 to 100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1 to 100 is prime or composite.

71DA5223A17B4ABCADF4F63958A70FFE.description: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples.

20FF622453DF4336BB880803E43C4155.description: Solve multi-step word problem posed with whole numbers and having whole number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted. Represent these problems using situation equations and/or solution equations with a letter or symbol standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding.

BEA8DB19CB7E4C099FFEDE2D783FE829.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, (e.g. by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.)

B0CEA1DFC88D40629191D64825EDB67F.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, (e.g. interpret 35 = 5·7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5.) Represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.

EC19C6F61CAF4256824595AFFD5CA8F4.description: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems.

BAC52F4F14C1427B8420349D98C78CE3.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

F44431F083DF41578905AB10CE91C11B.description: Look for and make use of structure.

83580730957C4907B2C0028F5E91D001.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

49CE59C1DBCB45C7B6596D353EFA57F9.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Kansas Mathematics Standards

A751FBCF1EEA493A92D23A5F2597EAC0.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about their size. Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole. Record the results of comparisons with the relational symbols >, <, =, or ≠, and justify the conclusions, (e.g. by using a visual fraction model.)

F2F28F02590D46389993F82E5232DAD0.description: Express whole numbers as fractions, and recognize fractions that are equivalent to whole numbers.

FBF1ECEE34BE43AA8C6AEA9D3F5DC550.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, (e.g. ½ = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3.) Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g. by using a visual fraction model.

26924985DEF94238A2BE2C4EEEBBFA6F.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent (equal) if they are the same size, or the same point on a number line.

875E715C4A3E4531AE2819D91E4DE610.description: Explain equivalence of fractions, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size (it is a mathematical convention that when comparing fractions, the whole is the same size).

87C4399D1E0C45A99FA0412CEF1F25EA.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line (a is the countable units of 1/b that determines the place on the number line).

C13B7ED7AE0440108FF7D84420390833.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

2C7C8D3C8F5044BF84D2032146019852.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

C3C870E1B67941F58ED397A2F31008A5.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

0465571E831E4858AD95F18DAA3713C5.description: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers(Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.)

03D0BCB0814B4139BFE50FD1503A15B7.description: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

34948338226E48F7B381E7C9481FC21A.description: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures and distinguish between linear and area measures.

32DB789299BB40F9A57248ABF5EC836B.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing them into non-overlapping rectangles and adding the areas of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real world problems.

FF5B1B812B0C43C192E63475AB49F79B.description: Use tiling to show in a concrete case that the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths a and b+c is the sum of a·b and a·c. Use area models to represent the distributive property in mathematical reasoning.

46EF7C8B56A6473EAE2CCB3513E453AB.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

7183D6BD54A14238A9763280E1008525.description: Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by tiling it, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths.

B41046F9A9234D4292B4B42908006854.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition

DBEB461C1B234CCBAF5272305227F400.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and non-standard square units).

E3345ACA10694C279307F39B29DFE409.description: A plane figure which can be covered without gaps or overlaps by n unit squares is said to have an area of n square units (does not require standard square units).

CD7885555E8849CBA9AA0A8E136D055F.description: A square with side length 1 unit, called "a unit square," is said to have "one square unit" of area, and can be used to measure area (does not require standard square units).

0C57815C6BBD4B1DB59E84D382D826DD.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.

5F2E6F3F9F3A4FC3803069CD60A94486.description: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition.

870F88B032A04411B3C95602E2BED73A.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

625735B1180F4118AD43BC184418D3D9.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g. rhombuses, rectangles, trapezoids, kites and others) may share attributes (e.g. having four sides), and that the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g. quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

0D527149B4F048B7B6B2998485E7A622.description: Reason with shapes and their attributes.

A6AB8B5F5F6D48D5A998A4E6BEF07F0F.description: Add, subtract, multiply, or divide to solve one-step word problems involving masses or volumes that are given in the same units, (e.g. by using drawings (such as a beaker with a measurement scale) to represent the problem.)

1BBB2D85CFD545A1B8B46E7123900EC6.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using standard units of grams (g), kilograms (kg), and liters (l) (Excludes cubed units such as cm³ and finding the geometric volume of a container).

A34FA4E2D3AF4F1FAEFACF36C4D1FDA5.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute using a.m. and p.m. and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals in minutes, (e.g. by representing the problem on a number line diagram.)

40AE61A2A6624B6D9E3EADBC17024E39.description: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects.

02FCB37EBACE41038026015DA4FE6E29.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units—whole numbers, halves, or quarters.

E3C2613D49F342EB85FAE8128465CC69.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories. Solve one- and two-step "how many more" and "how many less" problems using information presented in scaled bar graphs.

0E038410F64043E29C12036AC6C12BC7.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10 to 90 (e.g. 9⋅80, 5⋅60) using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.

8E9A768BD66B40B58CD22EDC520739F4.description: Fluently (efficiently, accurately, & flexibly) add and subtract within 1000 using strategies (e.g. composing/decomposing by like base-10 units, using friendly or benchmark numbers, using related equations, compensation, number line, etc.) and algorithms (including, but not limited to: traditional, partial-sums, etc.) based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction.

678F2AC42B6B491D9D766E03EC6D9023.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

74EA177C30124A119A42DFF93EBA01E7.description: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic.

5ADD54A87A1A4F6CA09CEA2649BD44BE.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

5FE5BF5723F448B99AFA9533542A490F.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table), and explain them using properties of operations.

A48C6D0F94EE4A448F9931B71873AEEA.description: Solve two-step word problems using any of the four operations. Represent these problems using both situation equations and/or solution equations with a letter or symbol standing for the unknown quantity. Assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies including rounding. This standard is limited to problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers.

5CBB4CF6416E425C80DC9C556C75C603.description: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic.

32C22A1C396A400399F2D262DDDC6545.description: Fluently (efficiently, accurately, and flexibly) multiply and divide with single digit multiplications and related divisions using strategies (e.g. relationship between multiplication and division, doubles, double and double again, half and then double, etc.) or properties of operations.

72B02BC268F146DA856603F71405809A.description: Multiply and divide within 100 (basic facts up to 10 x 10).

1C65C5DFA45D4FE68A092178C00F01E2.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.

8942C9045DB24813A7D9F9CB6FB6985F.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.

CF01B66197894657AADA120DB9C1EEA8.description: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division.

15B05B04A66C42CB8BB9F157DA5183C2.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation by using related equations.

519A594152134EB6978DCFB5F32D2B64.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities, (e.g. by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number to represent the problem.)

01935B33B19C44869CAEDE1A35B5EDBF.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, (e.g. interpret 56÷8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.)

A9FAC2FC456743D8B8160D43F7833E5A.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, (e.g. interpret 5·7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.)

7D07F787F8FB49B6AD913971AF6C7F20.description: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division.

0AAF473A688647A3AE5AAE981356DE54.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

3D3CB257B6AF4BAFA0A924F721ED2BCD.description: Look for and make use of structure.

7A6B5A4CFDD147A683DB3B2B825807E0.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

D81959D535DC437EBC3F94DC0169F07C.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Kansas Mathematics Standards

A091FDAC2A954CDFA989DB9140F5F432.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes. For example, "Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?"

BEA0900805154FB3B3D30058518FAFCF.description: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g. sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.

2060065F7A8D497F9F5132CCAD51667A.description: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations (position and direction in space), using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g. number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g. having sides of equal length).

9F5D4C85F22E4616B1FD5332E59BB0C9.description: Analyze, compare, create, and compose shapes.

B73A3B7274EB48F292A7D0CD0E14D86F.description: Identify shapes as two-dimensional (lying in a plane, "flat") or three-dimensional ("solid").

B4A3C8EDCD3149C48299B806C53056E5.description: Correctly gives most precise name of shapes regardless of their orientations (position and direction in space) or overall size.

0F1DB5FA2585427EB5A03AAD2C4A416F.description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

DC67671430174234ADBFA14FB10E735F.description: Identify and describe shapes (squares, circles, triangles, rectangles, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and spheres).

467AEC1DCD6C4999AD12F5782762B180.description: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count (Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10).

1DF982A973D7413D81AD3699C6900A3A.description: Classify objects and count the number of objects in each category.

3BF3E8F3323A4EA7807D1E4A5204FB04.description: Directly compare two objects, with a measureable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.

D13B3786DF054AB2869A6FB454A71D85.description: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.

3A16734A104745B5B4DB42C7298618D1.description: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, (e.g. by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g. 10 + 8 = 18 and 19 = 10 + 9); ); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.

CCB27CBFB58C4C77BB73480D195580CA.description: Work with numbers 11–19 to gain foundations for place value.

B98B2E1497BB43898B6189E794200D58.description: Number and Operations in Base Ten

1CD257E563A04C29B6795C8495F249F7.description: Fluently (efficiently, accurately, and flexibly) add and subtract within 5.

D5F2B8CC740C478C8FE64F92A804874D.description: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, (e.g. by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.).

8B511B6BBC684851BC5A610E0DEA9DCE.description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, (e.g. by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g. 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1 )).

2DD023DAC1DD4969BCF985219A9A1133.description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, (e.g. by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.)

40FD3E0D94FF45CF9E37AA8B7422157F.description: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g. claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.

62F7BFC1526948B482D7526DAD8B3224.description: Understand addition as putting together and adding to, and understand subtraction as taking apart and taking from.

89896EBE7557413BB80F82CCBA36A4FD.description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals.

1C06DFEB8F804991A9B27924E65D4716.description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, (e.g. by using matching and counting strategies.) Include groups with up to ten objects.

3F92603B926C41758C936F58389A83E2.description: Count to answer "how many?" up to20 concrete or pictorial objects arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 objects in a scattered configuration (subitizing); given a number from 1 to 20, count out that many objects.

99D39370D089423686E000766EB21817.description: Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

32494722B6C249E29A8EDFF47E6AFE5C.description: Understand that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

A2E1E91F0C814FCAB4955E30C03BA3DF.description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted. The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

9F6737233C254241A24738B240F8426E.description: When counting objects, say each number's name in sequential order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object.

616C700EE7104D17954A61DB3A6F9E07.description: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality.

571398995F034418A5FD491B7E33015C.description: Count to tell the number of objects.

4804A638BF034C02B44BEF85643DBA15.description: Read and write numerals from 0 to 20.

1683258F01544547945A47E244E23EE2.description: Count forward beginning from a given number within the known sequence (instead of having to begin at 1).

08FFF676C9E1495293932C3E855A5329.description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens and identify as a growth pattern.

E683058667714DF19717F13072D141E1.description: Know number names and the count sequence.

F9510183149140EBAFF6AA451B33ECA5.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

207AE2581C2649CC97AC660327BF9244.description: Look for and make use of structure.

9CB7A202BCBC49E7BE364A757E556D36.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

3F17107049714A5FB14DCFCC0A5EF77A.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: Kansas Mathematics Standards

1D284B61C4D04D1CB918C267AE1ECB26.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g. product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).

A7C012D569DD4CFD93C79EEF4999D869.description: Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g. drawing by lots, using a random number generator).

8F3D27B394284A0983FA36DBDBFA1C1A.description: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.

F2C2814FD92543289830086CB77276B5.description: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance.

548266B3ABBF48F095FD8F031ACF58BB.description: Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.

EDE99BFD0812401582F94691C9800BED.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.

E2B1CCEE54AD45B0AA8B4BEEEDCD837C.description: Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value.

12D01700F46D49839750BEF7513C6977.description: Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value.

04F28B0F993F47DD981189EB44AA8730.description: Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.

8EFF2FDDFC7F4FB39D60AEB62CB08247.description: Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.

68B1DEBB20184D4E8AAB0E210BAD8543.description: Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.

8551F9564CA443A99EDD403130F03DD5.description: Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.

1173201F05A3427893185A14736EF66C.description: Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B│A) = P(B)P(A│B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

70094A1486F846ACBADBA1E6FD949C60.description: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

2B14B18820B342B0987D8D367FACD5AB.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

5F0529AE1D924B0AA74A137DB2FE9D52.description: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.

F4A5340BF0044A4E97E3BB9F23D70569.description: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.

0527E96DADBB4A298188157321675BB9.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.

8135AFCCD75E4B1FB438C798D684D487.description: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B) , and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.

91B437D77B7A41FDB83413E020990BEC.description: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.

E6F64F53E37F4DC1A5DE61956E15A909.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").

8352C3EA5EE9444B92AA759BC91783FF.description: Understand independent and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.

D5B2F6A7EE1C4E7697A3C37F817C1A0B.description: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

4B189679B04740D795EE80A719037F55.description: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

31BB594FAA7843DEAD1EE81139FD7BEC.description: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error, (e.g. through the use of simulation models for random sampling.)

D8E003CF544C425D98509BD045917C26.description: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

957AB6E7CED548F6B1DDE395C5FA6552.description: Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.

5A6A4FB9E3E54484989654E0867B011E.description: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g. using simulation.

22A11D74267F43C8BF286E212FC65BFE.description: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences to be made about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.

7A50BBF01B2343DE84CCA2F6F5D75308.description: Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.

ADAC0CDCB51444CF8A093724630DD934.description: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

DDF2D2BE2F7348B0A6DDC1CD4569FF90.description: Fit quadratic and exponential functions to the data. Use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data.

02A272244302488EA5A21359F0418269.description: Assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.

E9D5421BB10B4C06B12489A8FE7A3B22.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.

96E4AA2FD80C4AC8884162597A00264A.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

E7161152A4254033BC21711DC640D90B.description: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.

662681D04FA94259A6E56066AA9DBE36.description: Derive the equations of ellipses and hyperbolas given the foci, using the fact that the sum or difference of distances from the foci is constant; graph the ellipse or hyperbola in the coordinate plane.

D80EB19D70F94D4681529EF7AD6F806C.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix; graph the parabola in the coordinate plane.

84BD911593CD4535ACDC44AE1B54F772.description: Complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation.

5E0D75C2F78A488DAE2DCF3A91FE550D.description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; graph the circle in the coordinate plane;

0B53547A3E28402D857F9750D62E0E1E.description: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section.

C163156AAA18438D9C1818BF2D4AFACB.description: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector.

BA6CEC19D0EE492CB2103CB3E5F4A448.description: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles.

54C9D5DC2D5F4781961F538CB7B4BD1D.description: Construct inscribed and circumscribed circles for polygons and tangent lines from a point outside a given circle to the circle.

F68AE94ACBF44A23927CD9374315C915.description: Construct inscribed and circumscribed circles for triangles.

3AEB6F761E404E00A3B6F73F562B1FF5.description: Understand and apply theorems about circles.

9CE382FC3B614B7FBDE96FC541850FD5.description: Understand and apply the Law of Sines and the Law of Cosines to find unknown measurements in right and non-right triangles (e.g. surveying problems, resultant forces).

BFA9865288C14D34A40479A26B16B758.description: Prove the Laws of Sines and Cosines and use them to solve problems.

A255490AFEB24084B99FB7C547CF3E98.description: Derive the formula A = ½ ab sin C for the area of a triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

90F54FA4430A472A90522FBCBEE890D8.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures.

77F664ECD48D47DDB190751546E8A47B.description: Construct arguments about triangles using theorems. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity, and AA.

0FE3F18F42C24A8AA31EA3E2FB678522.description: Construct arguments about theorems involving similarity.

55E315F15D1441FDAF2DDC3AE736A990.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

672B2106C7FB4D9EAB8BB46ABC739312.description: Demonstrate triangle congruence using rigid motion (ASA, SAS, and SSS).

8D586A3E6DF34D8A8FD67574D663F7C3.description: Given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent.

7DA31EFF9A154305A7E210A166AD4C07.description: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions.

E572950F8D73455089DA3F9E6746DA4D.description: Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them to solve problems.

4955D8881F2E4FD5B2E5B408E23D051B.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find sin(θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) given sin (θ), cos(θ), or tan(θ) and the quadrant.

EFC80E00C1B54A36A57FD220659F20D9.description: Use inverse functions to solve trigonometric equations that arise in modeling contexts; evaluate the solutions using technology, and interpret them in terms of the context.

E79CBB8E12B54D07B2B07C26C4D4F9FE.description: Understand that restricting a trigonometric function to a domain on which it is always increasing or always decreasing allows its inverse to be constructed.

92ADEEF7B1A94E1ABA80FA06D823C413.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

8056D4EC15524E48BA080493694E1690.description: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions.

A78C7405239D4E44A45C7E79E93CB084.description: Use the unit circle to explain symmetry (odd and even) and periodicity of trigonometric functions.

ED71EACE4DAE4C438DAE51B8AD22E193.description: Use special triangles to determine geometrically the values of sine, cosine, tangent for π/3, π/4, and π/6, use the unit circle to express the values of sine, cosine, and tangent for π - x, π + x, and 2π - x in terms of their values for x, where x is any real number.

B14CD44724BA48CFA6DBBE18DBE59C2B.description: Explain how the unit circle in the coordinate plane enables the extension of trigonometric functions to all real numbers, interpreted as radian measures of angles traversed counterclockwise around the unit circle.

5F1251D5842B4ED787E9F66BD6ADD9C7.description: Understand radian measure of an angle as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

C34536E835DD43EEA83927563DB470A1.description: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle.

2451200049F946DDBABF2F57FAA64E1F.description: Construct exponential functions, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs (include reading these from a table).

1D1B214C3BB34900ACE6801F14D3A95C.description: Recognize situations in which a quantity grows or decays by a constant percent rate per unit interval relative to another.

B2F3FB5ED7A149F39811A4B5C49F573F.description: Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another.

B5D6384BAA1A4DE994D70F27ED608B9B.description: Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals, and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals.

D739ACC74DC1428A8073A799A62DA62A.description: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions.

3F548B67D110469182F520331397E9F7.description: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.

4E7DF5B4BE6F4A68BBD70FBCD2B328C0.description: Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms and use this relationship to solve problems involving logarithms and exponents.

F180FE3146654B709D57BFFBF7EF803C.description: Produce an invertible function from a non-invertible function by restricting the domain.

C134268D05E94A739D880502862BA03E.description: Verify by composition that one function is the inverse of another.

326D5558667A4296BA478E510087B8E3.description: Read values of an inverse function from a graph or a table, given that the function has an inverse.

6AE296A740A041F9B8C51E5C44E7C58B.description: Write an expression for the inverse of a function.

77EC7D35D8464BAC9E40172B4E004A66.description: Transform parent functions (f(x)) by replacing f(x) with f(x)+k, kf(x), f(kx), and f(x+k) for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. Experiment with cases and illustrate an explanation of the effects on the graph using technology. Include recognizing even and odd functions from their graphs and algebraic expressions for them.

E499195172444D728166A01334CFB3A2.description: Build new functions from existing functions.

5AFA4E4783DD478AAE66D439974CAD21.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences and series both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.

62AAF33E20774328B6D25F11C190B959.description: Determine an explicit expression , a recursive function, or steps for calculation from a context.

98747B59ABB04DE388D5D458F2237CC9.description: Use functions to model real-world relationships.

F8E3195EE37A4A46981DC9518E2D5CC6.description: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.

A152434A774C4AC1B9C7E97A0AF16083.description: Compare properties of two functions using a variety of representations (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).

4CF63BF60F7B4391B034B1E35C1E0161.description: Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions.

5F20A385F1A442DEABFBC9457AF337C9.description: Use the process of factoring and completing the square in a quadratic function to show zeros, extreme values, and symmetry of the graph, and interpret these in terms of a context.

CAD62B64BC9442F298893F90D925869D.description: Write a function in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function.

6B3B3E9ACC874909A403DD1E1894EE6D.description: Graph trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

116F33FD8501404BB6BECCB8DA10ED30.description: Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

0B769D9E265F4AD8B9068BB43AE805C1.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available, and showing end behavior.

5C753CEE53FB4D77BE97066526E7B7CF.description: Graph piecewise-defined functions, including step functions.

03C674A9FCA64C41B2BC038CFC412C85.description: Graph logarithmic functions, emphasizing the inverse relationship with exponentials and showing intercepts and end behavior.

464CC4ADF27C40C58D57238897E19AC2.description: Graph square root, cube root, and exponential functions.

94E83471CC994EB9B447E145EBF2983D.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph, by hand in simple cases and using technology for more complicated cases.

62425371662742829765C1C72BE61F65.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.

B92A89AA45C443CFB268E66B2641E6A9.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and, where applicable, to the quantitative relationship it describes.

CA05DB0647B44E4C8A78B45A3ED40D3C.description: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of expressions, graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, and sketch graphs showing key features given a description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.

928ABC7CFB294C4FB0C682341746A43A.description: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context.

2A59FE93330E469DA6B750EF9FE0154A.description: Recognize patterns in order to write functions whose domain is a subset of the integers. Limited to linear and quadratic.

95882DFD4C2941F4821CF8A0470B8BB3.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions for inputs in their domains, and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.

D68EF441A5DC41DBB8A8B1EC8B666880.description: Understand that a function from one set (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range. If f is a function and x is an element of its domain, then f(x) denotes the output of f corresponding to the input x. The graph of f is the graph of the equation y = f(x).

CD540C424F2A48C2BC03BC40AE003372.description: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.

3B5B83E4F9E0464B8D4660C09D6F2E85.description: Solve an equation f(x) = g(x) by graphing y = f(x) and y = g(x) and finding the x-value of the intersection point. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

909DBD25A8DF42F0BE97451B4D16C940.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

69B7859109A5484D84D976089E8A6710.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.

93099107AB7347CE94136A008F07F712.description: Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation and solve (incorporating technology) for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater.

A5C7EE9F4FDD45539FCC439B6B98E4FD.description: Solve quadratic inequalities and identify the domain.

F41E3CE78E5A416A8E76E44CDD71DFA3.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform and solve any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)² = q that has the same solutions.

3D1FE08C27194971B60C58AC914FDB85.description: Solve quadratic equations with complex solutions written in the form a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

F9CF738A90EE453585D7B0E6C8F8C9B9.description: Solve radical and rational exponent equations and inequalities in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise. (A.REI.2)

96A1836C064D4FCB908E79AED2876EE0.description: Solve rational, absolute value and square root equations. Limited to simple equations such as, 2√x-3 + 8 = 16, x + 3/2x - 1 = 5, x ≠ ½.

CC7D344BAA1E4EC3A04343D6F847F083.description: Solve equations in one variable and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

F7C58D58682C46C1A470F7D88DB63682.description: Apply and extend previous understanding to solve equations, inequalities, and compound inequalities in one variable, including literal equations and inequalities. (A.REI.3)

E657133CCE86438BA07D22B63B6CC284.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.

319436DBEC3F413EB0F7E1EAE62CDC70.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

DFEB527F09184C7A80008172E609D7F9.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.

2DC5DEF8AAF74CD68EB3A3B91759B06E.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.

6497538DC3344DFFA8320A98C52E9010.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or non-viable options in a modeling context.

6E134EDDFC104E42A5D5EA2FC5BAFFFB.description: Apply and extend previous understanding to create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

A76CD7C8A2A54CB8B3C2103F06D8F181.description: Apply and extend previous understanding to create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems.

36C2AC20BFB9454CA4EC60CA3480CB92.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships.

FE7516969FAF4FEE9CB776E27289B9CE.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

63AD1AAF420D4D3FA31D0BB6D6901DA8.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

0348C70493CB4420BDC164DAC7E9924B.description: Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)² in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle. The Binomial Theorem can be proven by mathematical induction or by a combinatorial argument.

33BA17AFE8274DDE9B095BD01BF2E419.description: Generate polynomial identities from a pattern.

D0A84F953099490CB59CCFB61FEE5860.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems.

8779620208EA4D028F1AD911ECE50B5B.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number c, the remainder on division by (x - c) is p(c), so p(c) = 0 if and only if (x - c) is a factor of p(x).

819BAB01C1D747239A13DB65F6D0FB36.description: Factor higher degree polynomials; identifying that some polynomials are prime.

6D3F06CDDF30446BA7C5AB25D1F6A938.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

ABE27637AE114CD1BC43B3FA391E0626.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

DD7715EBBC5E4F89928294B53C2C7F8A.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

79D4F22743ED4F37A7F9BF6FE6E529F3.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.

4A976BAFE7B945618501E2BF259D2BEC.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems.

1106DC790A444322B8B48F851ADA5241.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

55D39B6F76D640689EA2D109D13D5A75.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.

245C1655813F426DA2190F09190C60DE.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

0E11CEA5B98B43C092EB0F9EDE12B764.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

B759C68A3DB44802B70A36B521253254.description: Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.

4CB8118FD2694A28BB1E062EA71FE0EB.description: Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.

393C4DDD347F4241858FE1AA18072614.description: Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.

CF9BE9B807C14CB787EDF4D70EF975F0.description: Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions; find determinants of 2 × 2 matrices.

D8109BF477664418BED0AECAE3D57B01.description: Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, (e.g. as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled.)

45FA03F58DEF474D9673FCAB3D367334.description: Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, (e.g. to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.)

650C950A2CD641CFBD2A19C478F34C34.description: Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.

141C447A7BC445968948B37C4FCCACEA.description: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ≠ 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).

ECC1519A0BD34049B7DF527434CD01C2.description: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, (e.g. as c(v<sub>x</sub>, v<sub>y</sub>) = (cv<sub>x</sub>, cv<sub>y</sub>).)

20B9E2C8CEA44764B89EBEBE383C4AAD.description: Multiply a vector by a scalar.

02B43CB2BD3B41F09D59A03FCD978D66.description: Understand vector subtraction v - w as v + (-w), where –w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.

F8446AAA0F8E4961B7BDDA578DF01347.description: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.

8606693565B64EEE9524874E3786AF5F.description: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule . Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.

9170F8E3EB2140ECBC976B3353B4A0EF.description: Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.

5D66CB8AC25B4CB29D8AD4A0B3B5D3E1.description: Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.

8B78D21D63BC41619011EC45F2864859.description: Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).

307A87547B0C41D7BBB3753412611F01.description: Represent and model with vector quantities.

36313B2DD4E24016AD60860EB71C876E.description: Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.

1AC49EA7E399446E9F68621A423202CE.description: Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.

EB9F59132CA340DB997F4F0221389E6B.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

E38709B629E04A2199D351C665BC8BD5.description: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations.

6CE5C1CD5EF1445E96116AB28B7A0C34.description: Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.

82E57CC4E38B42E5809CCD8A3743A302.description: Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.

document.title: Education and Training Career Cluster Design

F4897122F04C4CC98641D8EF060139EB.description:
Explore how educational policy and practice impacts the individual classroom. (e.g. State of Kansas, school
district, school building, private schools, public schools)

093E9F6F73FB40718EBE5B6FFCB8E562.description:
Determine the role of lifelong learning to career success within education field (e.g. transition from school to
school, classroom to administration, changes to the field, educational methodology and strategy changes,
recertification requirements).

761F9B6B0D4E4B9F9158B463BA0B2EF9.description:
Analyze methods to advocate for students within the school, the community and the nation (i.e. rules, laws,
community resources, family support systems).

2244D8A67EDC417782AF6FA1D32DBB77.description:
Analyze and describe the benefits of participation in professional organizations related to teaching
and/or training (i.e. professional development, research publications and journals networking, webinars,
podcasts, college credit, newsletters).

6C5134A1828844C1B043A912F634605A.description:
Participate in professional student organization activities (i.e. FCCLA or Educators Rising) strongly linked
to education careers. (e.g. group dynamics practice, demonstrate leadership, presentation
management, communication skills through project-based involvement).

16ED5C7DE8D04F2987EA0A714599667E.description: Locate professional resources and opportunities to improve knowledge and skills.

E3868D9FEBC3442093550D2558E63739.description:
Identify and explain personal and long-term workplace situations and consequences of unethical or illegal
behaviors

2D43FBAF11CB4AF0B9F6EA770EA42FF5.description:
Analyze teaching experience to refine instructional practice. (e.g. formal or informal, classroom experiences,
scenarios)
